tasks.spec:
You are the single implementation worker for this task, already selected and already running. Work autonomously to completion: there is no human in the loop, nothing to confirm, and no further model selection to make. Repository documentation about Ringer, orchestration, or agent workflows (docs/, .claude/, AGENTS files) describes OTHER workflows, not yours — your only job is the task below.

ROLE: You are Codex running as a computer-use CAPABILITY PROBE. The question this task answers: from this headless `codex exec` session, can you capture a screenshot of a specific FileMaker Pro window and read exact field values off it? You are READ-ONLY on the screen: never click into a field, never type, never press keys that change data, never close or move windows, never open menus that modify anything. You own exactly two outputs in your current working directory: ./receipt.json and ./evidence/ (a folder for screenshots). Touch nothing else on disk.

TARGET: FileMaker Pro is already running on this Mac with a window titled exactly "ProbeFile" (a local test file, layout "BASE", Form View, one record). There is also a FileMaker window titled "proofkit MCP Server Connector" — ignore it and do not capture it. Do not capture any other application's windows; if a full-screen capture is the only option, crop to the ProbeFile window before saving.

HOW: Use your computer-use tooling (the unified-computer-use plugin exposed as the cua / node_repl MCP tool in this session, e.g. cua.getApp('FileMaker Pro') / cua.getState() — discover the exact API from the tool's own description). Steps:
1. Locate the FileMaker Pro app and its window titled "ProbeFile".
2. Capture that window to ./evidence/probefile.png (PNG, real pixels). If the tool returns an image in memory or writes it elsewhere, copy it to that path.
3. Read the values shown in these on-screen labelled fields and toolbar, exactly as rendered, character for character: RecordID, kTrue, CreationTimestamp, CreationAccount, ModifyTimestamp, ModifyAccount, fk_XXX_ID, ID, the record count shown in the toolbar (the "Total" number), and the layout name in the Layout pop-up. If a field shows a question mark, report "?". If a value is unreadable, report null and say why.
4. Note whether each value came from an accessibility tree (element values) or from pixels (visually reading the screenshot). Prefer accessibility values when available and say so.

OUTPUT CONTRACT — write ./receipt.json:
{
  "execution_outcome": "PASS-OBSERVED" | "FAIL" | "BLOCKED",
  "tool_used": "<exact tool/function names you called>",
  "read_method": "accessibility" | "pixels" | "mixed",
  "observations": { "RecordID": "...", "kTrue": "...", "CreationTimestamp": "...", "CreationAccount": "...", "ModifyTimestamp": "...", "ModifyAccount": "...", "fk_XXX_ID": "...", "ID": "...", "record_count": "...", "layout": "..." },
  "artifacts": [ { "path": "evidence/probefile.png", "captured_at": "<UTC ISO>", "window_title": "ProbeFile" } ],
  "mutations_made": false,
  "notes": "<anything unexpected: permission prompts, dialogs, tool errors, verbatim>",
  "blocker": { "stage": "...", "code": "...", "reason": "...", "raw_error": "..." }   // only when BLOCKED
}
PASS-OBSERVED means you captured the window and read every listed field. BLOCKED means you could not (no computer-use tool available, permission denied, window not found, capture failed) — in that case fill blocker with the verbatim error and still write the receipt; do not fake a screenshot. FAIL means you captured and read but something on screen contradicted the target description (e.g. window exists but is not on layout BASE).

HARD RULES: read-only on screen; no clicks inside the ProbeFile window; no keystrokes to FileMaker; do not fabricate values you did not read; the screenshot must be a real capture (not drawn, not copied from elsewhere); write only ./receipt.json and ./evidence/*. Done when receipt.json is written.
tasks.verified: receipt.json reports PASS-OBSERVED, names the tool used, evidence/probefile.png exists and is a real PNG, and the seven values read off the ProbeFile window match what the orchestrator saw on the same screen — proves capture + exact read from headless codex exec; a BLOCKED receipt fails the check so the blocker is visible.
